candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.5 (c. 350 AD)

'And we know that the Son of God is come, and hath given us an understanding, that we may know him that is true, and we are in him that is true, even in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God, and eternal life' — Athanasius marks houtos estin ho alēthinos theos kai zōē aiōnios (THIS is the true God and eternal life) as the MOST EXPLICIT EXPLICIT-DEITY-OF-THE-SON Johannine-Catholic-Epistle anchor. The houtos (THIS — referring back to Jesus Christ in the immediately-preceding phrase) directly-names Christ as ho alēthinos theos (THE TRUE God, with definite article + qualifying-adjective). The Arians could not Arian-accommodate this without breaking standard Greek; Athanasius cites it as definitive against any creature-Christology.
